options: Sends an HTTP GET request to a URL and returns a response object
Reads a local CSV file from disk
Only works with government APIs, no others
Automatically converts a response into a DataFrame with no further code
questions.explain: requests is Python's standard library for calling REST APIs.

questions.q: What does a 200 status code mean?
options: The request succeeded
The resource doesn't exist
The server crashed
The request is still pending
questions.explain: 404 means not found, 429 means rate-limited, 500 means server error — 200 is success.

questions.q: Why does checking status_code matter separately from Lesson 19's exception handling?
options: Exceptions catch things that crash your code outright; status codes tell you a request completed but didn't necessarily succeed
They are exactly the same thing with no real difference
Status codes are only relevant for file reading, not APIs
Checking status_code replaces the need for try/except entirely
questions.explain: A request can 'complete' without crashing, yet still fail — that's what status codes reveal.

questions.q: Why does pagination typically use a while loop rather than a for loop?
options: You don't know in advance how many pages of data there are, until an empty page signals you're done
for loops cannot make HTTP requests
while loops are always faster than for loops
Pagination never actually requires any kind of loop
questions.explain: This is exactly the open-ended repetition scenario Lesson 17 introduced while loops for.

questions.q: How does a JSON API response commonly convert into a Pandas DataFrame?
options: response.json() returns a list of dictionaries — the same shape Lesson 21 already builds a DataFrame from directly with pd.DataFrame()
API responses can never be converted into DataFrames
You must manually retype every value before creating a DataFrame
Only CSV responses can become DataFrames, never JSON
questions.explain: requests fetches the data; pd.DataFrame() turns the resulting list of dicts into a real table, just like Lesson 21.
